uncited: Style and Content Adaptation modifies a pre-trained radiance field to incorporate specific visual styles or object contents by leveraging external conditions, such as reference images or text prompts, during the optimization loop.

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [SKED](12268-sked.md) and [Single-Image Textual Inversion](19221-single-image-textual-inversion.md) by explicitly using reference images as conditional priors to guide the diffusion model's denoising process, ensuring the generated content adheres to the visual characteristics of the reference rather than relying solely on textual descriptions or single-view embeddings.
The family shares a common optimization framework where a frozen diffusion model (typically Stable Diffusion) provides gradient signals to update the radiance field parameters.

The core mechanism involves rendering an image from the current radiance field state, passing it through the diffusion model to compute a Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) loss or similar gradient, and backpropagating this signal to the radiance field.

The key differentiator for this family is the conditioning mechanism: instead of using only a text prompt, the diffusion model is conditioned on a reference image $I_{ref}$ alongside the text prompt $T$.

This is typically achieved by concatenating the reference image features or using it as an additional input to the UNet's cross-attention or spatial attention layers, thereby constraining the generated noise prediction to match the style or content of $I_{ref}$.
SKED [12268-sked.md] focuses on localized 3D editing using multi-view 2D sketches as spatial priors.

It minimizes a composite loss $L = L_{SDS} + \lambda_s L_{sil} + \lambda_p L_{pres}$, where $L_{SDS}$ steers the content via diffusion, $L_{sil}$ ensures the rendered silhouette matches the sketch mask $M_v$, and $L_{pres}$ maintains fidelity to the original scene outside the sketch regions.
It is chosen when precise spatial control over object insertion or replacement is required.

By utilizing reference images as conditions, the method ensures that the generated content (e.g., "a stone chair") closely resembles the visual characteristics (material, texture) of the reference image (e.g., a stone), compared to results generated without a reference.

This is implemented by incorporating the reference image into the diffusion model's conditioning pipeline, often via cross-attention or feature concatenation, to transfer style attributes to the radiance field optimization.
The concept of using external priors for radiance field editing and generation has evolved from text-only guidance to multi-modal conditioning.
This approach addresses the limitations of text-only prompts, which may lack the precision required for specific material or stylistic replication.
